item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 01
item.description:
Verse 1

तपः स्वाध्याय निरताम् तपस्वी वाग्विदाम् वरम् | नारदम् परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिः मुनि पुंगवम् || १-१-१

Valmiki, devoted to austerity and self-study, asked Narada, the foremost among sages and the best among those skilled in speech.

Verse 2

कः नु अस्मिन् सांप्रतम् लोके गुणवान् कः च वीर्यवान् | धर्मज्ञः च कृतज्ञः च सत्य वाक्यो धृढ व्रतः || १-१-२

Who in this world at the present time is endowed with virtues and strength? Who knows righteousness, who is grateful, who speaks the truth, and who is firm in his vows?

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 02
item.description:
Verse 1

नारदस्य तु तद्वाक्यम् श्रुत्वा वाक्य विशारदः | पूजयामास धर्मात्मा सह शिष्यो महामुनिः ||

On hearing the words of Narada, the great sage Valmiki, righteous in conduct and skilled in speech, honoured him together with his disciples.

Verse 2

यथावत् पूजितः तेन देवर्षिः नारदः तथा | आपृच्छैव अभ्यनुज्ञातः स जगाम विहायसम् ||

Thus properly honoured by Valmiki, the divine sage Narada, having taken leave and received permission, departed through the sky.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 03
item.description:
Verse 1

श्रुत्वा वस्तु समग्रम् तत् धर्मार्थ सहितम् हितम् | व्यक्तम् अन्वेषते भूयो यद्वृत्तम् तस्य धीमतः || १-३-१

Having heard that complete account, containing Dharma, Artha, and what is beneficial, the sage again sought in detail the events concerning that wise Rama.

Verse 2

उपस्पृश्य उदकम् सम्यक् मुनिः स्थित्वा कृताञ्जलिः | प्राचीन अग्रेषु दर्भेषु धर्मेण अन्वेषते गतिम् || १-३-२

Having properly touched the water and stood with folded hands, the sage sat upon sacred darbha grass with its tips facing east and, through his spiritual insight, sought the course of the events.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 05
item.description:
Bala Kanda — Sarga 05

Verse 1

सर्वा पूर्वम् इयम् येषाम् आसीत् कृत्स्ना वसुंधरा | प्रजपतिम् उपादाय नृपाणम् जय शालिनाम् ||

Formerly, this entire earth belonged to those victorious kings, beginning with Prajapati.

Verse 2

येषाम् स सगरो नाम सागरो येन खानितः | षष्टिः पुत्र सहस्राणि यम् यान्तम् पर्यवारयन् ||

Among them was King Sagara, after whom the ocean was named, and whom sixty thousand sons accompanied when he set out.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 06
item.description:
Bala Kanda — Sarga 06

Verse 1

तस्यां पुर्यामयोध्यायां वेदवित्सर्वसंग्रहः | दीर्घदर्शी महातेजाः पौरजानपदप्रियः || १-६-१

In that city of Ayodhya lived one who was learned in the Vedas, possessed of every resource, far-seeing, greatly radiant, and beloved by both the citizens and the people of the countryside.

Verse 2

इक्ष्वाकूणामतिरथो यज्वा धर्मपरो वशी | महर्षिकल्पो राजर्षिस्त्रिषु लोकेषु विश्रुतः || १-६-२

Among the descendants of Ikshvaku, he was an excellent chariot-warrior, a performer of sacrifices, devoted to Dharma, self-controlled, like a great sage, and a royal sage renowned in the three worlds.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 08
item.description:
Verse 1

तस्य त्वेवम्प्रभावस्य धर्मज्ञस्य महात्मनः | सुतार्थं तप्यमानस्य नासीद्वंशकरः सुतः || १-८-१

That great-souled king, who possessed such qualities and was a knower of Dharma, had no son to continue his lineage, though he longed intensely for one.

Verse 2

चिन्तयानस्य तस्यैवं बुद्धिरासीन्महात्मनः | सुतार्थं वाजिमेधेन किमर्थं न यजाम्यहम् || १-८-२

As the great-souled king reflected upon this matter, the following thought arose in his mind: “Why should I not perform the Ashvamedha sacrifice for the sake of obtaining a son?”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 09
item.description:
Verse 1

एतत् श्रुत्वा रहः सूतो राजानम् इदम् अब्रवीत् | श्रूयताम् तत् पुरा वृत्तम् पुराणे च मया श्रुतम् || १-९-१

Having heard this, Sumantra, the charioteer, spoke to the king privately:

“Listen to an ancient account that I have heard from the Purana.”

Verse 2

ऋत्विग्भिः उपदिष्टोऽयम् पुरा वृत्तो मया श्रुतः | सनत्कुमारो भगवान् पूर्वम् कथितवान् कथाम् || १-९-२

ऋषीणाम् सन्निधौ राजन् तव पुत्राअगमम् प्रति |

“O King, I have heard this ancient account as it was related by the priests. The divine Sanatkumara formerly narrated this story in the presence of sages concerning the coming of your sons.”

एतत् श्रुत्वा रहः सूतो राजानम् इदम् अब्रवीत् | श्रूयताम् तत् पुरा वृत्तम् पुराणे च मया श्रुतम् || १-९-१

Having heard this, Sumantra, the charioteer, spoke to the king privately:

“Listen to an ancient account that I have heard from the Purana.”

Verse 2

ऋत्विग्भिः उपदिष्टोऽयम् पुरा वृत्तो मया श्रुतः | सनत्कुमारो भगवान् पूर्वम् कथितवान् कथाम् || १-९-२

ऋषीणाम् सन्निधौ राजन् तव पुत्राअगमम् प्रति |

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 12
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः काले बहु तिथे कस्मिन् चित् सुमनोहरे | वसन्ते समनुप्राप्ते राज्ञो यष्टुम् मनोऽभवत् || १-१२-१

After some time had passed, when the pleasant season of spring had arrived, King Dasharatha desired to perform the Vedic sacrifice.

Verse 2

ततः प्रणम्य शिरसा तम् विप्रम् देव वर्णिनम् | यज्ञाय वरयामास संतान अर्थम् कुलस्य च || १-१२-२

Then, bowing his head before that Brahmana sage Rishyasringa, whose splendour was like that of a deity, King Dasharatha requested him to conduct the sacrifice for the sake of obtaining progeny and continuing his royal lineage.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 15
item.description:
Verse 1

मेधावी तु ततो ध्यात्वा स किञ्चिदिदमुत्तरम् । लब्धसंज्ञस्ततस्तं तु वेदज्ञो नृपमब्रवीत् ॥

Then the wise and learned Rishyasringa, knowing the Vedas, reflected for a while and, having determined what was to be done, spoke to King Dasharatha.

Verse 2

इष्टिं तेऽहं करिष्यामि पुत्रीयां पुत्रकारणात् । अथर्वशिरसि प्रोक्तैर्मन्त्रैः सिद्धां विधानतः ॥

For the sake of obtaining sons, I shall perform the Putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice for you, according to the prescribed procedure, with the mantras taught in the Atharva Veda.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 16
item.description:
Verse 1

दशरथोऽथ हृष्टात्मा श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं मुनेः । ऋष्यशृङ्गं पुरस्कृत्य ययौ यष्टुं महायशाः ॥

Then King Dasharatha, delighted at heart after hearing the words of the sage, proceeded to perform the great sacrifice, placing Rishyasringa at the forefront.

Verse 2

स तु राजानमामन्त्र्य ऋष्यशृङ्गं पुरस्कृत्य च । सुमन्त्रं च महात्मानं मन्त्रिणं चेदमब्रवीत् ॥

After taking leave of the king and placing Rishyasringa at the forefront, the great sage Sumantra said these words to the minister:

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 17
item.description:
Verse 1

पुत्रत्वं तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः । उवाच देवताः सर्वाः स्वयंभूर्भगवानिदम् ॥

When Vishnu had attained the sonship of the great-souled King Dasharatha, Brahma, the self-created Lord, spoke these words to all the gods.

Verse 2

सत्यसंधस्य वीरस्य सर्वेषां नो हितैषिणः । विष्णोः सहायान् बलिनः सृजध्वं कामरूपिणः ॥

Create mighty companions for Vishnu, the truthful and heroic one, who desires the welfare of us all, and who are capable of assuming forms according to their will.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 17
item.description:
Verse 1

पुत्रत्वं तु गते विष्णौ राज्ञस्तस्य महात्मनः । उवाच देवताः सर्वाः स्वयंभूर्भगवानिदम् ॥

Create mighty companions for Vishnu, the truthful and heroic one, who desires the welfare of us all, and who are capable of assuming forms according to their will.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 19
item.description:
Verse 1

तच्छ्रुत्वा राजसिंहस्य वाक्यमद्भुतविस्तरम् । हृष्टरोमा महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत ॥

Having heard these wonderful and detailed words of King Dasharatha, the lion among kings, the greatly radiant Vishvamitra, with his hair standing on end with joy, spoke.

Verse 2

सदृशं राजशार्दूल तवैतद्भुवि नान्यथा । महावंशप्रसूतस्य वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिनः ॥

O tiger among kings, these words are befitting of you and no one else, for you are born in a great lineage and instructed by Vashishtha.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 19
item.description:
Verse 1

तच्छ्रुत्वा राजसिंहस्य वाक्यमद्भुतविस्तरम् । हृष्टरोमा महातेजा विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत ॥

Verse 2

सदृशं राजशार्दूल तवैतद्भुवि नान्यथा । महावंशप्रसूतस्य वसिष्ठव्यपदेशिनः ॥

O tiger among kings, these words are befitting of you and no one else, for you are born in a great lineage and instructed by Vashishtha.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 20
item.description:
Verse 1

तच्छ्रुत्वा राजशार्दूलो विश्वामित्रस्य भाषितम् । मुहूर्तमिव निःसंज्ञः संज्ञावानिदमब्रवीत् ॥

Having heard the words of Vishvamitra, the tiger among kings, Dasharatha became as if unconscious for a moment. Regaining his awareness, he spoke these words.

Verse 2

ऊनषोडशवर्षो मे रामो राजीवलोचनः । न युद्धयोग्यतामस्य पश्यामि सह राक्षसैः ॥

My lotus-eyed Rama is less than sixteen years old. I do not see him as fit to fight with the Rakshasas.

Verse 3

इयमक्षौहिणी पूर्णा यस्याहं पतिरीश्वरः । अनया सहितो गत्वा योद्धाहं तैर्निशाचरैः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 21
item.description:
Verse 1

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य स्नेहपर्याकुलाक्षरम् । समन्युः कौशिको वाक्यं प्रत्युवाच महीपतिम् ॥

Hearing the king’s words, which were filled with affection for his son, Vishvamitra, the son of Kusha, became angry and spoke to the lord of the earth.

Verse 2

पूर्वमर्थं प्रतिश्रुत्य प्रतिज्ञां हातुमिच्छसि । राघवाणामयुक्तोऽयं कुलस्यास्य विपर्ययः ॥

Having previously promised to fulfill my purpose, you now wish to abandon your promise. Such conduct is not proper for this lineage of the Raghus.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 23
item.description:
Verse 1

प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः । अभ्यभाषत काकुत्स्थौ शयानौ पर्णसंस्तरे ॥

When the night had passed and dawn appeared, the great sage Vishvamitra spoke to the two descendants of Kakutstha, Rama and Lakshmana, who were sleeping on a bed of leaves.

Verse 2

कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम पूर्वा सन्ध्या प्रवर्तते । उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम् ॥

“O Rama, Kausalya is blessed to have you as her son. The eastern dawn is appearing. Arise, O tiger among men; the morning duties to the gods are to be performed.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 25
item.description:
Verse 1

अथ तस्याप्रमेयस्य मुनेर्वचनमुत्तमम् । श्रुत्वा पुरुषशार्दूलः प्रत्युवाच शुभां गिरम् ॥

Having heard the excellent words of that sage of immeasurable power, Rama, the tiger among men, replied with auspicious words.

Verse 2

अल्पवीर्या यदा यक्षी श्रूयते मुनिपुङ्गव । कथं नागसहस्रस्य धारयत्यबला बलम् ॥

O foremost of sages, it is said that a Yakshi possesses little strength. How can this woman, being weak, possess the strength of a thousand elephants?

Verse 3

इत्युक्तं वचनं श्रुत्वा राघवस्यामितौजसः । हर्षयञ्छ्लक्ष्णया वाचा सलक्ष्मणमरिन्दमम् ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 26
item.description:
Verse 1

मुनेर्वचनमक्लीबं श्रुत्वा नरवरात्मजः । राघवः प्राञ्जलिर्भूत्वा प्रत्युवाच दृढव्रतः ॥

Having heard the firm and fearless words of the sage, Rama, the son of the best of men and firm in his vows, joined his palms and replied.

Verse 2

पितुर्वचननिर्देशात् पितुर्वचनगौरवात् । वचनं कौशिकस्येति कर्तव्यमविशङ्कया ॥

By the command of my father and out of reverence for my father’s word, I shall regard the command of Kaushika as something that must be carried out without hesitation.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 32
item.description:
## Verse 1

ब्रह्मयोनिर्महानासीद् कुशो नाम महातपाः ।

अक्लिष्टव्रतधर्मज्ञः सज्जनप्रतिपूजकः ॥

There was a great ascetic named Kusha, born from Brahma, who knew the duties of vows and righteousness and who honoured virtuous people.

## Verse 2

स महात्मा कुलीनायां युक्तायां सुमहाबलान् ।

वैदर्भ्यां जनयामास चतुरः सदृशान् सुतान् ॥

That great-souled Kusha begot four mighty and illustrious sons from a noble woman of the Vidarbha lineage.

## Verse 3

कुशाम्बं कुशनाभं च आसूर्तरजसं वसुम् ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 33
item.description:
## Verse 1

तस्य तद् वचनं श्रुत्वा कुशनाभस्य धीमतः ।

शिरोभिः चरणौ स्पृष्ट्वा कन्या शतम् अभाषत ॥

Having heard the words of the wise Kushanabha, the hundred maidens touched his feet with their heads and spoke to him.

## Verse 2

वायुः सर्वात्मको राजन् प्रधर्षयितुम् इच्छति ।

अशुभं मार्गम् आस्थाय न धर्मं प्रत्यवेक्षते ॥

“O King, the all-pervading Vayu desired to dishonour us. Resorting to an improper course, he paid no regard to righteousness.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 35
item.description:
Verse 1

उपास्य रात्रि शेषं तु शोणाकूले महर्षिभिः ।

निशायां सुप्रभातायां विश्वामित्रोऽभ्यभाषत ॥

Having spent the remaining part of the night on the bank of the river Sona with the great sages, Vishvamitra spoke when dawn had arrived.

Verse 2

सुप्रभाता निशा राम पूर्वा संध्या प्रवर्तते ।

उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते गमनायाभिरोचय ॥

“O Rama, the night has passed and dawn has appeared. The eastern twilight has begun. Arise, arise. May you be blessed. Prepare yourself for the journey.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 36
item.description:
Verse 1

उक्तवाक्ये मुनौ तस्मिन्नुभौ राघवलक्ष्मणौ ।

प्रतिनन्द्य कथां वीरावूचतुर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥

When the sage had finished speaking, the two heroic brothers, Rama and Lakshmana, praised the story and addressed the foremost of sages.

Verse 2

धर्मयुक्तमिदं ब्रह्मन् कथितं परमं त्वया ।

दुहितुः शैलराजस्य ज्येष्ठाय वक्तुमर्हसि ।

विस्तरं विस्तरज्ञोऽसि दिव्यमानुषसंभवम् ॥

“O Brahman, you have narrated this excellent account in accordance with righteousness. You are well versed in its details; therefore, please tell us in detail about the divine and earthly origin of the elder daughter of the king of mountains.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 40
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, Rama, together with Lakshmana, spoke these sweet words to the great sage.

Verse 2

भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि गङ्गावतरणं पुनः ।

भगीरथस्य च चरितं विस्तरेण महामुने ॥

“O Bhagavan, O great sage, I wish to hear once again about the descent of Ganga and the story of Bhagiratha in detail.”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 41
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा हृष्टरोमा च राघवः ।

उवाच परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, Rama was filled with delight and spoke with great pleasure to the great sage.

Verse 2

भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि गङ्गायाः सलिलं शुभम् ।

यथा त्रिपथगा जाता कथं च पतिता भुवि ॥

“O Bhagavan, I wish to hear how the sacred waters of Ganga became Tripathaga and how she descended upon the earth.”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 42
item.description:
Verse 1

कालधर्मं गते राम सगरे प्रकृतीजनाः ।

राजानं रोचयामासुरंशुमन्तं सुधार्मिकम् ॥

O Rama, when King Sagara passed away according to the law of Time, the ministers and people chose the highly righteous Anshuman as their king.

Verse 2

स राजा सुमहानासीदंशुमान् रघुनन्दन ।

तस्य पुत्रो महानासीद्दिलीप इति विश्रुतः ॥

O delight of the Raghu dynasty, Anshuman became a very great king, and he had a noble son who was renowned by the name Dilipa.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 43
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः सुरगणाः सर्वे ऋषयश्च तपोधनाः ।

भगीरथं महाराजं तुष्टुवुः सह पन्नगैः ॥

Then all the hosts of gods, together with the sages whose wealth was austerity and the Nagas, praised the great king Bhagiratha.

Verse 2

गङ्गा च सरितां श्रेष्ठा तं राजानमनुव्रता ।

जगाम सरितां श्रेष्ठा समुद्रं सरितां पतिम् ॥

Ganga, the foremost of rivers, followed that king and proceeded toward the ocean, the lord of rivers.

Verse 3

ततः सागरमासाद्य गङ्गा लोकनमस्कृता ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 44
item.description:
Verse 1

ततो रामः स लक्ष्मणो विश्वामित्रेण धीमता ।

सहितो मुनिशार्दूलं गङ्गां पप्रच्छ राघवः ॥

Then Rama, together with Lakshmana and the wise Vishvamitra, asked the tiger among sages about Ganga.

Verse 2

भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि गङ्गायाः सरितां वराम् ।

त्रिपथां कथमाख्यातां कथं वा जाह्नवी शुभा ॥

“O Bhagavan, I wish to hear about Ganga, the foremost of rivers. Why is she known as Tripatha, and how did the auspicious Jahnavi come to be?”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 45
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः ।

उवाच परमप्रीतो विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, Rama, together with Lakshmana, became exceedingly pleased and spoke to the great sage Vishvamitra.

Verse 2

भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि देवासुरसमागमम् ।

यथा वृत्तं पुरा युद्धं तन्मे कथय सुव्रत ॥

“O Bhagavan, I wish to hear about the encounter between the gods and the Asuras. O righteous one, tell me how that ancient battle took place.”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 46
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा रामः कौतूहलान्वितः ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं मुनिं रघुकुलोद्वहम् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, Rama, filled with curiosity, spoke these sweet words to the sage, the descendant of the Raghu dynasty.

Verse 2

भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथां परमपावनीम् ।

ययातेरथ राजर्षेः कथयस्व महामुने ॥

“O Bhagavan, O great sage, I wish to hear the most sacred story of the royal sage Yayati. Please narrate it to me.”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 47
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा राघवः सह लक्ष्मणः ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं मुनिं रघुकुलोद्वहम् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, Rama, together with Lakshmana, spoke these sweet words to the sage, the descendant of the Raghu dynasty.

Verse 2

भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छामि कथां परमपावनीम् ।

ययातेर्नहुषस्यैव चरितं मे वद प्रभो ॥

“O Bhagavan, I wish to hear the most sacred story. O Lord, tell me the story of Yayati and Nahusha.”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 48
item.description:
Verse 1

पृष्ट्वा तु कुशलं तत्र परस्पर समागमे ।

कथान्ते सुमतिः वाक्यं व्याजहार महामुनिम् ॥

After meeting one another there and enquiring about each other’s welfare, King Sumati spoke to the great sage Vishvamitra.

Verse 2

इमौ कुमारौ भद्रं ते देव तुल्य पराक्रमौ ।

गज सिंह गती वीरौ शार्दूल वृषभ उपमौ ॥

These two young princes are heroic, possessing strength equal to that of the gods. Their movements are like elephants and lions, and they resemble tigers and bulls in valour.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 49
item.description:
Verse 1

अफलस्तु ततश्शक्रो देवानग्निपुरोगमान् ।

अब्रवीत्त्रस्तनयनः सिद्धगन्धर्वचारणान् ॥

Then Indra, deprived of his testicles and with frightened eyes, spoke to the gods, Siddhas, Gandharvas and Charanas, with Agni at their head.

Verse 2

कुर्वता तपसो विघ्नं गौतमस्य महात्मनः ।

क्रोधमुत्पाद्य हि मया सुरकार्यमिदं कृतम् ॥

“By creating an obstacle to the austerities of the great-souled Gautama and arousing his anger, I have indeed accomplished this task for the gods.”

Verse 3

न च मेऽत्र विचारोऽस्ति यदिदं तपसः फलम् ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 50
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रागुत्तरां गत्वा रामः सौमित्रिणा सह ।

विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य यज्ञवाटमुपागमत् ॥

Then Rama, together with Lakshmana and led by Vishvamitra, proceeded toward the northeast and approached the sacrificial enclosure of King Janaka.

Verse 2

रामस्तु मुनिशार्दूलमुवाच सहलक्ष्मणः ।

साध्वी यज्ञसमृद्धिर्हि जनकस्य महात्मनः ॥

Rama, together with Lakshmana, said to Vishvamitra, the tiger among sages, “The sacrificial arrangements of the great-souled Janaka are indeed excellent and abundant.”

Verse 3

बहूनीह सहस्राणि नानादेश्निवासिनाम् ।

ब्राह्मणानां महाभाग वेदाध्ययनशालिनाम् ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 51
item.description:
Verse 1

जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा शतानन्दो महामुनिः ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् ॥

Hearing the words of Janaka, the great sage Shatananda spoke sweetly to the great sage Vishvamitra.

Verse 2

स्वागतं ते महामुने विश्वामित्र महायशः ।

कुशलं ते महाभाग कच्चित्ते कुशलं गृहे ॥

“O great sage Vishvamitra, greatly renowned one, welcome to you. O greatly fortunate one, I hope you are well and that everything is well in your hermitage.”

Verse 3

महातेजा महाप्राज्ञः कौशिकः कुशलं वदन् ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 52
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा हृष्टरोमा महातपाः ।

शतानन्दो महातेजा रामं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, the great ascetic Shatananda, whose hairs stood on end with joy, and who was greatly radiant, spoke to Rama.

Verse 2

अहो ते परमो लाभो महर्षेर्दर्शनं शुभम् ।

विश्वामित्रस्य काकुत्स्थ तपसा भावितात्मनः ॥

“O Kakutstha, your great fortune is that you have obtained the auspicious sight of the great sage Vishvamitra, whose self has been purified through austerity.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 53
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रवचः श्रुत्वा हर्षितो मुनिपुङ्गवः ।

शतानन्दो महातेजा रामं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥

Hearing the words of Vishvamitra, the great sage Shatananda, greatly radiant and filled with joy, spoke to Rama.

Verse 2

अहो ते कथितं सर्वं यथावृत्तं महात्मना ।

विश्वामित्रेण काकुत्स्थ वसिष्ठस्य च धीमतः ॥

“O Kakutstha, the great-souled Vishvamitra has narrated everything exactly as it happened, concerning himself and the wise Vasistha.”

Verse 3

राजर्षिरभवद्राजा विश्वामित्रो महाबलः ।

तस्याश्रमं समागम्य वसिष्ठो मुनिसत्तमः ॥

“Vishvamitra was a royal sage and a mighty king. The excellent sage Vasistha came to his hermitage.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 54
item.description:
Verse 1

कामधेनुं वसिष्ठोऽपि यदा न त्यजते मुनिः ।

तदास्य शबलां राम विश्वामित्रोऽन्वकर्षत ॥

When the sage Vasistha did not give up Kamadhenu, O Rama, Vishvamitra began to drag Shabala away.

Verse 2

नीयमाना तु शबला राम राज्ञा महात्मना ।

दुःखिता चिन्तयामास रुदती शोककर्शिता ॥

While being led away by the great king Vishvamitra, Shabala, distressed and afflicted with sorrow, began to lament and think.

Verse 3

परित्यक्ता वसिष्ठेन किमहं सुमहात्मना ।

या अहं राजभृतैर्दीना ह्रियेयं भृशदुःखिता ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 55
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः क्रुद्धो महातेजा ब्रह्मदण्डमनुत्तमम् ।

वसिष्ठो भगवान् प्रादाद्विश्वामित्राय धीमते ॥

Then the greatly radiant and venerable Vasistha gave the wise Vishvamitra the supreme Brahma-danda, the staff of Brahman.

Verse 2

तद् ब्रह्मदण्डं महत् तेजो ज्वलितं सर्वतोमुखम् ।

नाशयामास तद् घोरमस्त्रं ब्रह्मर्षिसत्तमः ॥

That mighty Brahma-danda, blazing with radiance on every side, destroyed that terrible weapon. The excellent Brahmarshi Vasistha neutralized it.

Verse 3

ततः क्रुद्धो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

ब्रह्मास्त्रम् अस्त्रविद् श्रेष्ठो मुमोच परमाद्भुतम् ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 56
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः परमसन्तुष्टो विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

ब्रह्मर्षित्वं समापन्नो वसिष्ठमुपगच्छत ॥

Then the great sage Vishvamitra, having become completely satisfied and having attained Brahmarshi-hood, approached Vasistha.

Verse 2

अभिवाद्य महात्मानं वसिष्ठं मुनिसत्तमम् ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ॥

Having bowed to the great-souled Vasistha, the excellent sage, the great sage Vishvamitra spoke sweet words.

Verse 3

ब्रह्मर्षिरस्मि भगवान् वसिष्ठस्य प्रसादतः ।

तत्सर्वमस्त्रं भगवन् मया प्राप्तं तपोबलात् ॥

“O venerable one, I am a Brahmarshi by the grace of Vasistha. Through the power of austerity, I have obtained all those weapons.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 57
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः संतप्तहृदयः स्मरन्निग्रहमात्मनः ।

विनिःश्वस्य विनिःश्वस्य कृतवैरः महात्मना ॥

Then Vishvamitra, remembering his humiliation by the great-souled Vasistha, became distressed at heart and repeatedly sighed, filled with resentment.

Verse 2

स दक्षिणां दिशं गत्वा महिष्या सह राघव ।

तताप परमं घोरं विश्वामित्रो महातपाः ॥

O Raghava, that great ascetic Vishvamitra went to the southern direction with his chief queen and performed extremely severe austerities.

Verse 3

फलमूलाशनो दान्तश्चचार महतं तपः ।

अथास्य जज्ञिरे पुत्राः सत्यधर्मपरायणाः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 58
item.description:
Verse 1

तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य त्रिशङ्कोर्विश्वामित्रस्तदा ।

अब्रवीन्नरशार्दूलं राजर्षिं तं तपोधनः ॥

Hearing the words of Trishanku, Vishvamitra, whose wealth was austerity, spoke to that royal sage, the tiger among men.

Verse 2

अलं भद्रं तवाख्यातं गमिष्यसि न संशयः ।

स्वशरीरेण राजेन्द्र देवानां परमां गतिम् ॥

“Enough. You have spoken well. O lord of kings, you shall certainly attain the highest abode of the gods with your own body. There is no doubt.”

Verse 3

तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 59
item.description:
Verse 1

त्रिशङ्कुं पतितं दृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रो महातपाः ।

अब्रवीत् कुपितो वाक्यं सर्वान् ऋषिगणान् प्रति ॥

Seeing Trishanku falling, the great ascetic Vishvamitra, becoming angry, spoke these words to all the groups of sages.

Verse 2

अहं ससृज्यमानं तु त्रिशङ्कोः स्वर्गमुत्तमम् ।

सृष्ट्वा लोकान् बहून् रम्यान् स्थापयिष्यामि शाश्वतान् ॥

“I shall create a supreme heaven for Trishanku. I shall create many beautiful worlds and establish them as eternal.”

Verse 3

ततो देवाः सगन्धर्वाः सिद्धाश्च परमर्षयः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 60
item.description:
Verse 1

एवमुक्तो वसिष्ठेन विश्वामित्रो महातपाः ।

प्रत्युवाच महातेजा वसिष्ठं मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥

Thus addressed by Vasistha, the great ascetic Vishvamitra, greatly radiant, replied to Vasistha, the foremost of sages.

Verse 2

यद्येवं वचनं सत्यं वसिष्ठस्य महात्मनः ।

तथापि मे न सन्देहो ब्रह्मर्षित्वे भविष्यति ॥

“Even if the words of the great-souled Vasistha are true, I shall nevertheless have no doubt that I will attain Brahmarshi-hood.”

Verse 3

इत्युक्त्वा स महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महातपाः ।

तपश्चचार घोरं वै कौशिकः परमात्मवान् ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 61
item.description:
Verse 1

गाधेः पुत्रो महातेजा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

कदाचित् कौशिकीतीरे तपस्तेपे महातपाः ॥

The greatly radiant Vishvamitra, son of Gadhi and the great sage, once performed severe austerities on the bank of the river Kaushiki.

Verse 2

तस्य तत्राश्रमपदे शुनःशेपो महामुनिः ।

आश्रमं मुनिशार्दूलमाजगाम महायशाः ॥

At that hermitage, the greatly renowned great sage Shunahshepa came to the hermitage of Vishvamitra, the tiger among sages.

Verse 3

शुनःशेपस्तु राजर्षेः पुत्रोऽभूद् भरतर्षभ ।

ऋचीकस्य महात्मनः पौत्रः सत्यपराक्रमः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 62
item.description:
Verse 1

शुनःशेपं नरश्रेष्ठं विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

रक्षार्थं तस्य राजर्षेः पुत्रान् स्वान् प्रत्यभाषत ॥

The great sage Vishvamitra spoke to his own sons for the protection of Shunahshepa, the best among men and the son of the royal sage.

Verse 2

पुत्रा वः शुनःशेपोऽयं शरणं शरणागतः ।

रक्ष्यतां सर्वथा पुत्रा मा वधिष्टं तपोधनाः ॥

“This Shunahshepa has come to me seeking refuge. O my sons, protect him in every way. Do not let him be killed, O you whose wealth is austerity.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 63
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रो महातेजाः स हि गाधिसुतो मुनिः ।

सिद्धाश्रमं समासाद्य तपश्चक्रे सुदारुणम् ॥

The greatly radiant Vishvamitra, the sage and son of Gadhi, reached Siddhashrama and performed extremely severe austerities.

Verse 2

तस्य तत्र तपस्तप्त्वा दीर्घकालं महामुनिः ।

ब्रह्मर्षित्वं महातेजाः प्राप्तुमैच्छन्महामुनिः ॥

The great and greatly radiant sage performed austerities there for a long time, desiring to attain Brahmarshi-hood.

Verse 3

ततः प्रीतमनाः शक्रो देवैः सह महर्षिभिः ।

विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो मुनिम् ॥

Then Indra, pleased in mind, came together with the gods and great sages to see the great-souled sage Vishvamitra.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 64
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रसादितो देवैर्विश्वामित्रो महातपाः ।

प्राप्तवान् परमं ब्रह्म ब्राह्मण्यं तपसा स्वयम् ॥

Then, having been pleased by the gods, the great ascetic Vishvamitra attained the supreme state of Brahmanhood through his own austerities.

Verse 2

ततः सुमहद् आश्चर्यं देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा ।

दृष्ट्वा विश्वामित्रतपः प्रशशंसुर्महामुनिम् ॥

Then the gods together with the groups of sages, seeing the great and wondrous austerities of Vishvamitra, praised the great sage.

Verse 3

ततो ब्रह्मा महातेजा विश्वामित्रं महामुनिम् ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 65
item.description:
Verse 1

विश्वामित्रो महातेजा देवान् सर्वानुवाच ह ।

ब्रह्मर्षित्वं मम प्राप्तं वसिष्ठेन महात्मना ॥

The greatly radiant Vishvamitra spoke to all the gods: “I have attained Brahmarshi-hood, accepted by the great-souled Vasistha.”

Verse 2

ततः प्रहृष्टमनसो देवाः सर्षिगणास्तथा ।

विश्वामित्रं महात्मानं तुष्टुवुर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् ॥

Then the gods together with the groups of sages, delighted in mind, praised the great-souled Vishvamitra, the foremost of sages.

Verse 3

सिद्धाश्च ऋषयश्चैव गन्धर्वाश्च महर्षयः ।

सर्वे ते मुनिशार्दूलं प्रशशंसुः पुनः पुनः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 66
item.description:
Verse 1

जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं रामं सत्यपराक्रमम् ॥

Hearing the words of Janaka, the great sage Vishvamitra spoke sweet words to Rama, who possessed true valour.

Verse 2

धनुर्दर्शय रामस्य कौशिकस्य महात्मनः ।

इत्युक्तो मुनिशार्दूलो जनकं प्रत्यभाषत ॥

“Show the bow to Rama.” Thus addressed, Janaka, the tiger among sages, replied.

Verse 3

इदं धनुर्वरं राजन् देवैर्दत्तं महात्मना ।

शैवं चापि महाबाहो त्र्यम्बकेण महात्मना ॥

“O king, this excellent bow was given by the gods. It is the great bow of Shiva, the mighty-armed one, the great-souled Tryambaka.”

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 67
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रहृष्टवदना जनकस्य महीपतेः ।

आहूय मन्त्रिणः सर्वान् प्रोवाच वचनं शुभम् ॥

Then King Janaka, with a delighted face, summoned all his ministers and spoke these auspicious words.

Verse 2

इदं धनुर्वरं दिव्यं मम पूर्वपितामहैः ।

पूजितं परमेशस्य त्र्यम्बकस्य महात्मनः ॥

“This divine and excellent bow was worshipped by my forefathers. It belonged to the great Lord Tryambaka, the Supreme One.”

Verse 3

न शक्यं मानुषैर्धर्तुं धनुरेतन्महाबलैः ।

न च देवैर्न गन्धर्वैर्नासुरैर्न च राक्षसैः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 68
item.description:
Verse 1

जनकेन समादिष्टा दूतास्ते क्लान्तवाहनाः ।

त्रिरात्रमुषिता मार्गे तेऽयोध्यां प्राविशन् पुरीम् ॥

Those messengers, commanded by Janaka, having rested for three nights on the way, entered the city of Ayodhya with their horses exhausted.

Verse 2

ते राजवचनाद् गत्वा राजवेश्म प्रविशिताः ।

ददृशुर्देवसंकाशं वृद्धं दशरथं नृपम् ॥

Having gone there according to the king’s command and entered the royal palace, they saw the aged King Dasharatha, radiant like a god.

Verse 3

बद्धाञ्जलिपुटाः सर्वे दूता विगतसाध्वसाः ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 69
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतकर्मा नराधिपः ।

विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य वसिष्ठं च महामुनिम् ॥

At dawn, after completing his morning duties, King Dasharatha set out with the great sage Vishvamitra and the great sage Vasistha leading the way.

Verse 2

ऋषीन् वसिष्ठप्रमुखान् पुरोधसं च मन्त्रिणः ।

पुत्रांश्च राजशार्दूलो गच्छन्तमन्वगच्छत ॥

The tiger among kings, accompanied by the sages headed by Vasistha, the royal priest and his ministers, followed by his sons, proceeded on the journey.

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 70
item.description:
Verse 1

जनकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा वसिष्ठो भगवानृषिः ।

विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य जनकं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥

Hearing the words of Janaka, the venerable sage Vasistha, with Vishvamitra before him, spoke to Janaka.

Verse 2

अव्यक्तप्रभवो ब्रह्मा शाश्वतो नित्य एव च ।

तस्य पुत्रो मरीचिस्तु मरीचेः कश्यपः सुतः ॥

Brahma is the eternal and everlasting source of the unmanifest. His son was Marichi, and Marichi’s son was Kashyapa.

Verse 3

विवस्वान् कश्यपाज्जज्ञे मनुर्वैवस्वतः स्मृतः ।

मनुः प्रजापतिः पूर्वमिक्ष्वाकुश्च मनोः सुतः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 72
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रभाते विमले कृतकर्मा नराधिपः ।

विश्वामित्रं पुरस्कृत्य वसिष्ठं च महामुनिम् ॥

At dawn, after completing his morning duties, the king, with Vishvamitra and the great sage Vasistha leading the way, proceeded onward.

Verse 2

ऋषीन् वसिष्ठप्रमुखान् पुरोधसं च मन्त्रिणः ।

पुत्रांश्च राजशार्दूलो गच्छन्तमन्वगच्छत ॥

The tiger among kings was accompanied by the sages headed by Vasistha, the royal priest, ministers, and his sons.

Verse 3

ततः प्रयाते दुर्धर्षे रामे कमललोचने ।

लक्ष्मणे च महाबाहौ राज्ञो दशरथस्य च ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 73
item.description:
Verse 1

प्रभाते तु ततः राजा दशरथो महामतिः ।

ऋषीन् सर्वान् समाहूय मन्त्रिभिश्च समन्वितः ॥

At dawn, the wise King Dasharatha summoned all the sages and was accompanied by his ministers.

Verse 2

वसिष्ठं वामदेवं च विश्वामित्रं च राघवः ।

अर्चयित्वा यथान्यायं प्रहृष्टो वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥

Dasharatha duly honoured Vasistha, Vamadeva and Vishvamitra, and then, being delighted, spoke these words.

Verse 3

अद्य मे सफलं जन्म दिष्ट्या मे सफलं तपः ।

यन्मे पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च दृष्टाः सर्वे समागताः ॥

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 74
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रागुदयात् संध्यामुपास्य मुनिपुङ्गवः ।

अग्निहोत्रं च विधिवत् कृत्वा जप्यं च नित्यशः ॥

Before sunrise, the foremost of sages performed the twilight prayers, duly performed the Agnihotra, and completed his daily recitations.

Verse 2

विश्वामित्रो महातेजा रामं दशरथात्मजम् ।

उवाच मधुरं वाक्यं धर्मयुक्तमिदं शुभम् ॥

The greatly radiant Vishvamitra spoke these sweet and auspicious words, consistent with righteousness, to Rama, the son of Dasharatha.

Verse 3

अद्य प्रभृति ते राम तपः स्वाध्यायसंयुतम् ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 75
item.description:
Verse 1

रामे चापि नरश्रेष्ठे जनकस्यात्मजे तदा ।

दिव्यं धनुर्वरं घोरं शङ्करस्य महात्मनः ॥

Then, when Rama, the foremost of men and son of Janaka, was present, the great and terrible divine bow of the mighty Shankara—

Verse 2

आनिनाय महातेजा जमदग्न्यः प्रतापवान् ।

तं दृष्ट्वा राघवः श्रीमान् विस्मयं परमं गतः ॥

—the greatly radiant and powerful son of Jamadagni brought it forth. Seeing it, the illustrious Raghava was exceedingly astonished.

Verse 3

स तु दृष्ट्वा महाबाहुं रामं दशरथात्मजम् ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 76
item.description:
Verse 1

अथ राजा दशरथो हृष्टः पुत्रमुपागतम् ।

दृष्ट्वा रामं महात्मानं प्रत्यनन्दत सादरम् ॥

Then King Dasharatha, delighted to see his great-souled son Rama who had returned, received him with great affection.

Verse 2

ततः स राजा काकुत्स्थः पुत्रैः सर्वैः समन्वितः ।

प्रविश्य नगरीं रम्यामयोध्यां मुदितोऽभवत् ॥

Then the Kakutstha king, accompanied by all his sons, entered the beautiful city of Ayodhya and became joyful.

Verse 3

ततो रामस्य चरितं श्रुत्वा सर्वे नराः पुरे ।

item.title: Ramayan — Bala Kanda — Sarga 77
item.description:
Verse 1

ततः प्रहृष्टः सुमन्त्रस्त्वरितो राजशासनात् ।

रामं प्रस्थापयामास वनवासाय राघवम् ॥

Then Sumantra, delighted and acting swiftly according to the king’s command, prepared Raghava Rama for departure to the forest.

Verse 2

रामस्तु पितुरादेशं शिरसा प्रतिपद्य च ।

वनं गन्तुं व्यवस्याथ सीतामामन्त्रयत्तदा ॥

Rama accepted his father’s command with bowed head and then resolved to go to the forest. He then spoke to Sita.

Verse 3

सीते वनं गमिष्यामि पितुराज्ञां न लङ्घये ।

त्वमत्रैव निवर्तस्व मम दुःखं न वर्धय ॥
